meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and was anyone going to speak to me before Owen saw it on his phone in the middle of class?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Why is the zero still in the gradebook, then, Hale?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Show me. Turn the screen around so I can read the timestamps myself. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so I want to see exactly what that history says and where it came from.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Okay. I'm writing that down, and I'll read the text myself before I say anything else, Hale. A wrong line in an essay is a wrong line; what else do you have that shows how it got there?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Okay. That's procedure 4.4, and I have it printed. I want it in writing today that nothing goes on his record, that no one from his class is in that room, and that the zero comes out of the gradebook now, not after Thursday.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged entering the zero before you called me and offered a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still require written confirmation today that nothing goes on his record, that no one from his class is in that room, and that the zero comes out of the gradebook now, not after Thursday. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the fallback position, with the rewrite offered but not accepted, and her terms still open.
What moved her: "I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong." Owning it in one sentence earned a flat okay and some ground.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked you to turn the screen, show her the version history on it before moving on to the second point, so she could check it herself.
